/10-day-sri-lanka-itinerary.lead: Enough days to see the shape of the island without treating it like a checklist.
/10-day-sri-lanka-itinerary.body:
Who this outline is for

Ten days is a sensible first visit: Cultural Triangle, Kandy and tea country, a wildlife park, then the south coast. LankaLux runs this as the Signature Sri Lanka Journey, always adjustable.

A calm ten-day shape

Arrive and sleep near Colombo. Move inland to Sigiriya and the ancient cities. Continue to Kandy, then into tea country toward Nuwara Eliya and Ella, often with a stretch by train. Descend to Yala for a safari, then the coast around Galle and Mirissa before you fly.

That is a sketch, not a prison timetable. A private chauffeur-guide makes the joins between regions human instead of heroic.

If you have fewer or more days

With a week, drop a region rather than rushing all of them. With two weeks, add a second park or more idle beach time. How many days do you need? is the fuller version of that advice.

See the day-by-day

The public Signature page has the detailed daily notes. Use it as inspiration; your dates, hotels and pace will still be written for you as a tailor-made tour.

Safari jeeps and park tickets are arranged separately unless stated.

/private-chauffeur-guide-sri-lanka.lead: One vehicle, one person who knows the roads, and a journey that can change when you want it to.
/private-chauffeur-guide-sri-lanka.heroAlt: LankaLux private vehicle in Sri Lanka
/private-chauffeur-guide-sri-lanka.body:
What a chauffeur-guide actually means

With LankaLux you do not collect a rental car, and you do not join a coach. You travel with a dedicated English-speaking chauffeur-guide and a private vehicle for the whole stay, including airport pickup and drop-off.

They drive, keep the days unhurried, and share context along the way: when to leave for a park gate, which stretch of coast is calmer that week, where a short stop is worth it. We describe this honestly as a chauffeur-guide, not as a licensed national-guide qualification.

Why travellers choose this over self-driving

Sri Lanka rewards curiosity and punishes tight schedules. Distances look small on a map. The chauffeur-guide absorbs the logistics so you can watch tea country go by, or ask to linger. Compare this with self-driving if you are still weighing the two.

The vehicle stays with you

The same car (or van) remains yours from arrival to departure. Families often prefer the Toyota Voxy; couples sometimes choose a sedan. See Our Fleet on the homepage, or ask us to match a vehicle to luggage and child seats.

What is and is not included

The chauffeur-guide, private vehicle, and airport transfers are part of the journey we plan. Train tickets, safari jeep hire, park entrance fees and optional activities are not included unless we specifically say so. We arrange them where we can; fees are paid separately or on site.

Ready to shape dates around this? Begin with a tailor-made itinerary or a journey idea.

/tailor-made-sri-lanka-tours.lead: A route written around your dates, your pace, and the kind of days you actually enjoy.
/tailor-made-sri-lanka-tours.heroAlt: Sri Lanka landscape for a tailor-made journey
/tailor-made-sri-lanka-tours.body:
Not a standard package

LankaLux does not sell a locked coach tour. We start with how you like to travel: slow mornings, wildlife before breakfast, a train through tea country, or more time by the water. The itinerary is written for you, then adjusted as the trip unfolds.

Our journey ideas are starting points, not cages. The Signature Sri Lanka Journey is a balanced first visit. Wildlife, hills or coast can lead instead.

How planning works

You share dates, who is coming, and a few preferences. We return a custom itinerary with a private chauffeur-guide, a vehicle for the stay, airport pickup and drop-off, and handpicked hotels or villas. Then we refine it together before you fly.

Private from arrival to departure

You are not waiting for a group. A chauffeur-guide stays with you, which makes last-minute changes simple: an extra hour at a temple, a beach afternoon instead of another drive.

Fees to expect beyond the journey plan

Train tickets, safari jeeps, park tickets and optional activities are arranged where possible but are not included unless stated.

Families may prefer a gentler version: Sri Lanka family tours. First-timers often start with our 10-day itinerary.

/sri-lanka-family-tours.lead: The island works well with children when the days are shorter, the car is comfortable, and nobody is watching a group clock.
/sri-lanka-family-tours.heroAlt: Family-friendly private vehicle in Sri Lanka
/sri-lanka-family-tours.body:
Why a private journey helps with children

A tailor-made family trip in Sri Lanka is mostly about pacing. With LankaLux you keep a private vehicle and an English-speaking chauffeur-guide for the stay, so a rest stop, an earlier hotel return, or a skipped viewpoint is ordinary, not a negotiation with a coach.

How we usually shape the days

We leave space between long drives, mix a cultural morning with an easy afternoon, and avoid stacking too many ticketed sites. Wildlife mornings are early; we plan a quiet midday after. The travelling with children note covers trains, parks and heat in more detail.

Vehicles

Families often travel in a Toyota Voxy: space for people and luggage without feeling like a minibus tour. Child seats can be discussed when you plan. See Our Fleet.

Starting points

A shortened Signature journey works for a first visit. Families who care more about animals than forts may prefer the wildlife journey, taken slowly. Coast days at Mirissa or near Galle give everyone a reset.

Park tickets, optional boat trips and some activities are paid separately unless we say otherwise. Tell us ages when you write; it changes the plan more than any slogan.

/destinations/ella.lead: Mist, tea, and a village that works best when you are not racing the clock.
/destinations/ella.heroAlt: Hill country near Ella, Sri Lanka
/destinations/ella.body:
Why visit

Ella sits in the hill country with views over tea and forested slopes. It is a natural pause after Kandy or Nuwara Eliya, and a centrepiece of the Hill Country and Scenic Rail Journey.

The train

Many travellers reach Ella by the hill-country train, one of the island's slow pleasures. Seats are arranged in advance where we can; tickets are a separate cost. Your chauffeur-guide typically meets you at the station. The train, explained covers what to expect.

How many nights

Two nights lets you walk a viewpoint at a civilised hour and keep an unhurried afternoon. Little Adam's Peak and Nine Arches are popular; we would rather you do one well than three in a rush.

Onward

From Ella you can descend toward Yala or the south coast. A tailor-made plan can linger in tea country if that is the point of the trip.

/destinations/galle.lead: A walled town on the south coast, best taken slowly after the inland roads.
/destinations/galle.body:
Why visit

Galle Fort is a UNESCO-listed old town of lanes, ramparts and a working harbour. It is the cultural pause in our Coastal Retreat Journey and the usual south-coast chapter of a ten-day outline.

What to do

Walk the ramparts at a cooler hour, look into courtyards, and keep the rest of the day uncluttered. The Fort is compact; it does not need a forced march. Nearby beaches offer a different pace the following day.

How many nights

Two nights in or near the Fort is enough for most travellers. Families sometimes stay a little outside for space and a pool, then visit the Fort without luggage.

Nearby

Mirissa is a short hop east for beach time and, in season, whale watching (an optional extra). Your chauffeur-guide makes that a simple morning rather than a relocation crisis.

/destinations/kandy.lead: The hill capital: a lake, a temple, and the start of tea country.
/destinations/kandy.body:
Why visit

Kandy sits in the hills with a lake at its centre and the Temple of the Tooth Relic as its most visited site. It is the hinge between the Cultural Triangle and tea country on our Signature and Hill Country journeys.

What to see

The temple is the usual focus. A circuit of the lake, a botanical garden if the group has energy, and an evening performance if you want one, are enough. Spice gardens on the road in are optional, not obligatory.

How many nights

One night works if you are moving. Two nights is kinder, especially after Sigiriya. From Kandy the scenic train toward Nuwara Eliya or Ella is the classic continuation.

Temple etiquette is simple: covered shoulders and knees, shoes off. Your chauffeur-guide will time arrival so you are not walking in the hardest heat.

/destinations/mirissa.lead: A south-coast pause: sand, boats in season, and permission to do very little.
/destinations/mirissa.body:
Why visit

Mirissa is a beach town on the south coast, used on the Coastal Retreat and as the unwind chapter of a Signature journey. After forts and parks, it is where the itinerary exhales.

Beach and optional boats

Most days here should be unscheduled. Whale watching is seasonal and optional; it is never guaranteed, and the boat fee is separate. Surfing and simple beach time need no itinerary language at all.

With Galle

Galle Fort is close enough for a half-day without changing hotels. A chauffeur-guide makes that a civilised loop rather than a luggage exercise.

How many nights? Two is a minimum if you have been inland all week. Families often want three. See south versus east coast timing if you are choosing a season.

/destinations/sigiriya.lead: The rock is famous. The day around it is what makes a visit civilised.
/destinations/sigiriya.heroAlt: Sigiriya Rock Fortress in Sri Lanka
/destinations/sigiriya.body:
Why visit

Sigiriya is a fifth-century rock fortress in the Cultural Triangle, with frescoes, terraced gardens and a wide view from the summit. It appears on our Signature journey because it gives first-time visitors a clear sense of Sri Lanka inland, without needing a specialist expedition.

What to see

Most travellers climb the rock in the cooler morning. The water gardens at the base, the lion paws, and the view over forested plains are the usual sequence. Nearby Dambulla cave temples and village landscapes pair well the same afternoon if you keep the pace kind.

How many nights

Two nights nearby is comfortable: one for the climb, one without an alarm. With a private chauffeur-guide you can leave the hotel at a sane hour and skip the bus-tour crush where possible.

Nearby

Polonnaruwa and Anuradhapura sit in the same region. Kandy is the natural next stop toward the hills. A tailor-made plan can emphasise ruins or move on quickly if heat is a concern, especially with children.

/destinations/udawalawe.lead: Open grassland, reservoirs, and elephants that do not require a rumour to find.
/destinations/udawalawe.body:
Why visit

Udawalawe is a national park of grassland and water, known for elephants. It is less crowded than Yala on many days and sits on the Nature and Wildlife Discovery Journey.

Safari notes

As at Yala, you leave the touring vehicle and take a jeep into the park. Jeep hire and entrance fees are separate unless stated.

Yala or Udawalawe?

If leopards are the dream, Yala is the usual answer. If you want reliable elephants and a slightly simpler day, Udawalawe is often the kinder park. The comparison is here: Yala vs Udawalawe.

Two nights is plenty for most families. Combine with Yala only if you have time; stacking parks on consecutive dawn starts tires everyone.

/destinations/yala.lead: Early gates, dry-zone light, and a jeep that is not a crowd.
/destinations/yala.heroAlt: Leopard habitat in Yala National Park
/destinations/yala.body:
Why visit

Yala is Sri Lanka's best-known national park for leopard sightings, with elephants, birds and a coastline of dunes. It sits on both the Signature and Nature and Wildlife journeys.

How a safari actually works

Park drives are in open safari jeeps with a tracker, not in your touring car. Your chauffeur-guide gets you to the lodge and the gate on time; the jeep is a separate arrangement. Train tickets, jeep hire and park entrance fees are not included unless we say so.

When to go

Dry months generally mean easier wildlife viewing. Some blocks close seasonally. We time drives for early morning and late afternoon. See best time to visit Sri Lanka and Yala versus Udawalawe.

How many nights

One night allows a single drive. Two nights, with a morning and an evening safari, is the more satisfying stay if wildlife is a reason for the trip.

/guides/best-time-to-visit-sri-lanka.h1: Best Time to Visit Sri Lanka
/guides/best-time-to-visit-sri-lanka.lead: The island has more than one climate. Choose a coast and a pace, then we write the days around that.
/guides/best-time-to-visit-sri-lanka.body:
There is no single perfect month

Sri Lanka has two monsoon systems. The south and west are generally drier in the northern winter months; the east often behaves differently later in the year. We plan around that, rather than pretending every week is beach weather everywhere.

South coast and Galle

For Galle and Mirissa, travellers often aim for the drier south-west season. A coastal retreat still works in shoulder months if you accept some rain and keep days unhurried.

Hill country

Tea country can be cool and misty in any season. That is part of the point of Ella and the hill-country train. Pack a layer; do not treat the highlands as a beach.

Wildlife

Dry months generally make game viewing easier. Some park blocks close seasonally. Yala versus Udawalawe matters as much as the month. Jeep hire and tickets remain separate unless stated.

Tell us your dates first. A tailor-made plan can emphasise the kinder coast rather than forcing a south-coast beach in the wrong week.

/guides/chauffeur-guide-vs-self-driving.lead: One person who knows the roads, or a rental car and a map. They are not the same holiday.
/guides/chauffeur-guide-vs-self-driving.heroAlt: LankaLux private vehicle in Sri Lanka
/guides/chauffeur-guide-vs-self-driving.body:
What LankaLux offers

You travel with a dedicated English-speaking chauffeur-guide and a private vehicle from airport to airport. They drive, keep the days unhurried, and share practical context: when to leave for a park gate, which stretch of coast is calmer that week. We describe this honestly as a chauffeur-guide, not as a licensed national-guide qualification.

What self-driving asks of you

Self-driving in Sri Lanka means local traffic patterns, rural night driving, parking at temples, and navigating around trains, tuk-tuks and unmarked turns. Some travellers enjoy that. Many first-time visitors find it uses the energy they wanted for the island itself.

Who a chauffeur-guide suits

Families, couples who want the train without luggage logistics, and anyone combining Sigiriya, the hills and a park in one trip. You can linger without renegotiating a hire car return. See Our Fleet if vehicle size matters.

What is still separate

Train tickets, safari jeep hire and park entrance fees are not included unless we say so. We arrange them where we can.

Ready to travel this way? Start with a tailor-made itinerary or a journey idea.

/guides/how-many-days-in-sri-lanka.h1: How Many Days Do You Need in Sri Lanka?
/guides/how-many-days-in-sri-lanka.lead: Enough time to see the shape of the island. Not so little that every day is a transfer.
/guides/how-many-days-in-sri-lanka.heroAlt: Sri Lanka journey landscape for planning trip length
/guides/how-many-days-in-sri-lanka.body:
The honest answer

Sri Lanka looks compact on a map. Distances are not. A private chauffeur-guide makes the joins human, but you still cannot do Sigiriya, the train, Yala and Galle as four frantic trophies in five nights.

Seven days

Choose two regions, not four. Culture and coast, or hills and a park, are both workable. Trying to “do the island” in a week usually means hotel corridors and a tired last morning.

Ten days

This is the length we recommend for most first visits. Cultural Triangle, Kandy and tea country, a safari, then the south. See the 10-day itinerary outline and the public Signature journey for a day-by-day sketch you can still change.

Two weeks

Add a second park only if wildlife is the point. Otherwise spend the extra nights doing less: another evening in Ella, a third beach day near Mirissa, or a slower climb at Sigiriya.

If you already have dates, a tailor-made itinerary is more useful than a generic packing list. Families should also read travelling with children.

/guides/sri-lanka-hill-country-train.lead: A slow pleasure through tea, not a commuter hop. Tickets are arranged; they are not bundled into the car.
/guides/sri-lanka-hill-country-train.heroAlt: Sri Lanka hill country landscape near the scenic train
/guides/sri-lanka-hill-country-train.body:
Why people talk about it

The hill-country line is one of the island's slow pleasures: tea terraces, mist, and a pace that matches Ella better than another highway transfer. It sits at the centre of the Hill Country and Scenic Rail Journey.

How we usually run it

Seats are arranged in advance where we can. Train tickets are a separate cost, not included in the chauffeur-guide journey unless we specifically say so. Your chauffeur-guide typically takes you to the station and meets you at the other end with the bags, so you are not managing luggage in the aisle.

Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Ella

Kandy is the usual starting hinge from the Cultural Triangle. Some travellers ride a shorter scenic stretch rather than the full popular segment if dates are tight. Little Adam's Peak and Nine Arches can wait for the following morning; the train is enough for one afternoon.

When it disappoints

It disappoints when it is treated as a must-photograph sprint, or when tickets are left to chance in high season. We would rather you skip it than stand. A tailor-made plan can replace the train with a tea-country drive if that is kinder for children or for mobility.

Continue from Ella toward Yala or the south coast, or linger if tea country is the point of the trip.

/guides/sri-lanka-with-children.lead: The island is generous with families if you stop treating it like an adult trophy hunt.
/guides/sri-lanka-with-children.heroAlt: Private van for family travel in Sri Lanka
/guides/sri-lanka-with-children.body:
Pace before highlights

Children remember a pool hour and a kind hotel more than a third temple. With LankaLux you keep a private vehicle and an English-speaking chauffeur-guide, so an earlier return or a skipped viewpoint is ordinary. See family tours for how we plan that.

How many days

Ten days still works if you drop something. A week needs two regions, not four. Read how many days in Sri Lanka and then cut further. Dawn safaris are optional, not mandatory.

Parks, forts and the train

Udawalawe is often gentler than a packed Yala morning. Galle Fort is compact if you keep it to a cooler hour. The hill-country train is a highlight if seats are arranged and someone meets you at the station with the bags.

The vehicle

Families often prefer a van such as the Toyota Voxy for space and child seats. Ask us to match luggage and seating on Our Fleet. We do not invent medical or visa advice; we plan the days around the ages you give us.

Safari jeeps and park tickets remain separate unless stated.

/guides/yala-vs-udawalawe.lead: Both are worth a dawn start. They are not interchangeable, and neither belongs in the touring car.
/guides/yala-vs-udawalawe.heroAlt: Wildlife in a Sri Lanka national park
/guides/yala-vs-udawalawe.body:
The short version

If leopards are the dream, Yala is the usual answer. If you want reliable elephants and often a simpler day, Udawalawe is frequently the kinder park. Sightings are never guaranteed in either.

How a safari actually works

You leave the touring vehicle. Park drives are in open jeeps with a tracker. Your chauffeur-guide gets you to the lodge and the gate; the jeep is a separate arrangement. Train tickets, jeep hire and park entrance fees are not included unless we say so.

How many nights

One night allows a single drive. Two nights, with a morning and an evening safari, is the more satisfying stay if wildlife is a reason for the trip. Stacking both parks on consecutive dawn starts tires everyone, especially children.

Which journey they sit on

Yala appears on the Signature and Nature and Wildlife journeys. Udawalawe is a centrepiece of the wildlife itinerary. A tailor-made trip can choose one park well rather than both poorly.
